finding: Knock Control's settled floor on KTuner is 0.49 (owners call 0.49-0.51 'zero'). Hondata's display floor reads about 0.54 for the same ECU state, so a Hondata owner's number is about 0.05 higher than the same thing on KTuner. Readings of 0.47-0.48 are momentary.
notes: Our 9 drives (108,878 moving rows): settled minimum 0.49 on every drive; 1,043 rows (1.0 %) dip below 0.48 (to 0.33-0.47) as 1-3 sample blips at throttle transitions (402 single-sample runs), plus one single-sample 0.70 spike at lift-off (aug22-0903 t=391 s). So 0.47 reports (civicxi-148) are transients, not a lower floor. Hondata 0.54 vs KTuner 0.49: four sources, display offset, not engine behaviour (civic11forum-43). ktuner-forum-5 is a 2.0 CVT (T3).

finding: Since KTuner 1.0.6.2 Knock Control is set to exactly 0.59 after a flash and learns down with driving; older reports of 0.6-0.9 after a flash or on the stock calibration predate that change.
log_channel: Knock Control (first minutes after a Flash)
notes: Primary: raw/ktuner-official/version_history.md, Version 1.0.6.2, '16-17 Civic 1.5T All: Knock Control Now Starts At .59 After A Flash'. Our data: aug30-1529 first logged sample is 0.59 exactly, settles to 0.49; kc-after-flash says 'around 0.58' (drive summary value). The card's <= 0.60 rule is right; the number to quote is KTuner's 0.59. civicx-108 (stock cal 0.9 'normal for factory', Dec 2017) is pre-1.0.6.2 history; aug30-1509 (3.6 s idle log, 0.77) is too short to read.

finding: Forum 'scale' for Knock Control: 0.49-0.53 outstanding, up to ~0.70 normal under hard load or heat, 0.69+ 'danger zone' (hearsay from Phearable), ~0.8 power loss you can feel, 0.85 'not damage, just less timing', 0.9+ irregular (KTuner staff, search excerpt), > 1.0 concerning (one tuner: 'likely a bent rod'). The labels disagree with each other; none comes with evidence.
notes: Converted with this car's boosted retard table (fact-check §2: cost = 10.2 x (score - 0.49)): 0.53 = 0.4 deg, 0.59 = 1.0, 0.69/0.70 = 2.0-2.1, 0.80 = 3.2, 0.85 = 3.7, 0.90 = 4.2, 1.00 = 5.2 deg. kc-ranges' Stop 0.80 sits where youtube-14 says power loss is felt and below the 0.9 'irregular' line, so nothing contradicts the card; the forum ladder is context, never a limit. 'Max 1.0, cannot retard further' (civicx-61, search excerpt) vs KTuner staff seeing 0.8 -> 1.2 on an Element turbo (ktuner-forum-57, T3, other ECU): unsettled, irrelevant at our 0.65 peak. 'Bent rod above 1.0' is second-hand and the owner's own counter-example (fresh fuel fixed it) undercuts it.

finding: 'On 91 octane expect Knock Control near 0.9, on better premium 0.5-0.6' (attributed to KTuner).
notes: Refuted by our data: on E10 RON95 (about US 90-91, the same class) Starter 21 cool drives sit 0.49-0.54 and the hottest traffic drive peaks 0.65. Also refuted by other 91-octane owners on 21 psi maps: youtube-33 (max 0.52 on 91, Canada) and civicxi-109 (~0.49 at 21 psi on 91). Probably pre-1.0.6.2 stock-calibration behaviour (civicx-108). Never quote it.

finding: KTuner's formula: final ignition = Ignition table + Knock Ignition Limitation - Knock Retard, and the ECU uses the lesser of that and the Ignition table; Knock Retard = Knock Control x Knock Retard table (example 0.38 x 10 = 3.8 deg; 21 + 2 - 3.8 = 19.2 deg).
ktuner_setting: Ignition Base (read only); Knock Ignition Limit and Knock Retard tables are not in the owner's file
notes: Already carried by kc-ignition-formula, kc-ranges and fact-check §2. Physics cross-check from a T1 owner log: civic11forum-26 retard 9-10 at KC 0.8+ and ~6 at 0.56 implies a table of ~11-12 deg, the same order as our 10.2.

finding: Low logged ignition at WOT on a base map (about 0 deg) is not uncommon: several tables decide final timing and base maps leave room (KTuner staff).
notes: Our logs agree: Ignition logs -1.5 to +0.5 deg at boost onset (1,600-2,500 rpm, aug22-0903) and only 3.5-4.5 deg at 16 psi, 4,900-5,550 rpm, with Knock Control at 0.49-0.52. That is the map (Ignition Base has 150 negative cells, kc-timing-percent), not knock. Owner symptom 'my timing is near zero under boost' -> answer: normal on this map; judge Knock Control, not the absolute degrees.

finding: Logged values are stepped: KTuner says Knock Retard is logged rounded (3.8 shows as 3.5) and Actual Ignition is rounded 'on OBD platforms' (19.2 shows as 19). On this car's TunerView (V2) logs both Ignition and Knock Retard move in 0.5 deg steps and Knock Control in 0.01 steps.
notes: All 108,918 logged rows: Ignition and Knock Retard are multiples of 0.5 (43 % of Ignition rows end in .5), Knock Control multiples of 0.01. So the '1 deg' ignition step in KTuner's example (and fact-check §2's '(0.5 deg and 1 deg)') is the OBD-logger case, not V2. KTuner's 3.8 -> 3.5 shows truncation, not rounding; our boosted pairs fit truncation with a ~10.25 deg table or rounding with ~10.0 deg equally (337 vs 331 of 360 rows), so the true boosted table is ~10.0-10.5 deg, consistent with 10.2. Consequence: under boost every score from 0.49 to 0.54 logs Knock Retard 5.0, so a 0.05 score change (~0.5 deg) is invisible in Knock Retard: read Knock Control, and keep 0.5 deg as the noise floor (kc-fuel-test already does).

finding: Knock Control is the ECU's always-active, global adaptation to fuel quality and environment (heat, load), not a per-event knock reading; if it climbs on every pull the ECU is detecting knock and the timing is too aggressive for the fuel.
notes: KTuner staff (ktuner-forum-1): 'a product of your fuel quality and your environmental factors'; Phearable about its own tunes (vendors-27); ECUTek already cited in fact-check §2. Matches CONTEXT.md's Fuel-quality score definition.

finding: Knock Count is not knock on this platform: it tracks the ECU's misfire-style monitor, accrues at startup, shifts and throttle changes, and dozens over a drive mean nothing; only a steep count (50+ in a few seconds) with a flashing CEL or P0300 matters. Knock Count and Knock Control are separate ECU systems.
ktuner_setting: Disables/Monitors: Misfire Monitor (enabled on this car)
log_channel: not in the owner's logs (no Knock Count channel); CEL / P0300
notes: Adds the one threshold the card lacks: 'steep count, 50+ in seconds, CEL flashing' (D-Rob via civicxi-136; KTuner staff civicxi-60: 41 total is nothing, the CEL is the alert). Owner examples: 37 counts in 15 min, 8 in 68 mi, 5 in 4 mi, all with KC at 0.49-0.55 and no fault.

finding: Owner theory: 'Knock Retard drives Knock Control; KC only rises once retard passes ~5.0 (5.5 gives 0.55, 6.5 gives 0.65)'.
notes: Backwards. KTuner's formula (g2-05) makes retard the product of KC and the table, and our logs show 5.0 deg retard scheduled at the 0.49 floor under boost (fact-check §2). The apparent 'retard 5.5 -> KC 0.55' pattern is just the ~10 deg table seen through rounding. The card's sentence 'the 5.0 degrees ... is scheduled from the score, not knock events' is the answer.

finding: Logged Knock Retard of 5-8 deg on WOT pulls that falls to zero at lift-off, with Knock Control near the floor, is the schedule, not knock; KC can read 0.7 with under 1 deg of retard in light-load cells; 10+ deg pulled on every pull (KC near 1.0 under boost) is a real problem.
notes: Our data: retard 5.0 at 0.49 under boost, 2-5 deg table in cruise cells, ~11 deg in the 1,500 rpm lugging cell (fact-check §2). 10+ deg every pull = score ~1.0 on our 10.2 deg table, far beyond our 0.80 Stop. civic11forum-62's 'ECU often adds fuel before retarding' is unverified and not used.

finding: Honda's non-Si 1.5T ECUs raise Knock Control on purpose above about 5,200-5,400 rpm, whatever the knock sensor sees; values drop back to ~0.49 at cruise. KTuner names the behaviour in its own release notes ('Artificial Knock Control Rise'), including for 'Civic 1.5T 2022+' codebases that have it.
ktuner_setting: Quick Enables: Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise
notes: Primary: version_history.md 1.0.11.0 under 'Civic 1.5T 2022+': 'Artificial Knock Control Rise Disable Option For Codebases That Have It'. Our car: one excursion above 5,200 rpm in 9 drives (aug22-0903, 0.8 s to 5,555 rpm): KC 0.50 -> 0.52, too short to show the rise. Side dispute: 10th-gen sources say Si ECUs lack it (civicx-127, civicxi-138) while civic11forum-30/41 report it on 11th-gen Si stock tunes; irrelevant here (FE is non-Si). Category note: civicx-117 is a fuel-octane comparison (91 vs 94) that also shows the rise.

finding: KTuner offers a checkbox that removes the forced rise: Quick Enables -> 'Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise' (added 1.0.10.1 for 16-21 non-Si, 1.0.11.0 for 2022+ codebases that have it, extended to more 16-21 ECUs in 1.0.11.9). On base/Starter maps the owner chooses it; Phearable 1.5R race files remove it, TSP Stage 1 and base Phearable 1.5 keep it. On this car (KTuner 1.0.14.0, Starter 21 Dual Tune 2) the box is OFF, so the rise is present.
ktuner_setting: Quick Enables: Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise (off on this car)
notes: Our car's state: .scratch/downpipe-power/issues/11-quick-adjustments-screenshot.md (KTuner 1.0.14.0 screenshots, 23 Aug 2026): 'Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise off'. This refutes the second-hand 'KTuner Starter maps also remove it' ([F7], ignition-from-datalog.md, low) for this map. Rule change: the >5,200 rpm exclusion in kc-high-rpm is correct for this car today but must be conditional on the box; if the owner ticks it (a setting, not a table; the app never writes it), high-rpm rises become real knock and must count (g2-14). Record the box state in the Car profile. civicx-58 (search excerpt, another group's category): Phearable 1.5R Race MAF reduced the rise on a 16 CVT.

finding: With the artificial rise removed, Knock Control above 5,200 rpm only rises on detected knock: owners report 0.49-0.52 up to 6,000-6,500 rpm on 91, and any rise is then real knock to act on (US remedy: a splash of E85).
ktuner_setting: Quick Enables: Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise
notes: Caveat: 10th-gen CVT on US 91; E85 is not sold at Vietnamese pumps, our equivalent is E10 RON97 III tested tank vs tank (kc-fuel-test). Upgrade to Supported once one owner pull above 5,500 rpm is logged with the box ticked.

finding: Size of the forced rise: about +0.20 per pull above 5,300 rpm (to 0.70-0.94 on repeated or long pulls, even on 93/94), costing only about 1.5-2 deg past 5,500 rpm.
ktuner_setting: Quick Enables: Eliminate Artificial Knock Control Rise
notes: Physics check with our boosted table: 0.20 x 10.2 = 2.0 deg, matching civicx-3's 1.5-2 deg. Reported peaks 0.72 (93, 6k), 0.89 (stock), 0.93-0.94 (TSP Stage 1). Gives kc-high-rpm a cost in degrees: a forced rise to ~0.7 costs ~2 deg, only at the top of the rev range.

finding: Knock Control rises at low rpm under load (about 1,250-1,500 rpm) on CVT 1.5T cars, including a hot-climate Indonesian non-Si CVT on RON90 (retard up to 18, KC avg 0.72 at 1,250-1,500 rpm) and US CVTs reaching 0.65-1.0 at 1,400 rpm; owners advise not flooring below ~3,000 rpm (LSPI).
ktuner_setting: no map change (habit); the Indonesian fix (ignition -0.2 in that zone, fuel-cut delay, MAF calibration) is out-of-scope (context)
log_channel: Knock Control vs Engine RPM 900-1,700 with TPS/MAP high
notes: Our data: 31 of 41 score rises happened while lugging at 900-1,700 rpm, and the map's implied retard table is ~11 deg at 1,500 rpm / -1 psi (fact-check §2, kc-oil). The boostedgamester CVT (civicx-102) is a big-turbo flex car: caveat. civicxi-141 is the closest twin in the whole crawl (SE Asia heat, CVT, low RON); later plug gap 0.7 mm + heat shield made his edits unnecessary. thresholds.json boost_raise_min_rpm 3000 already encodes the 3,000 rpm advice.

finding: Knock Control learns back down within minutes of calm driving: steady light load in a high gear near atmospheric manifold pressure (40-50 mph), not lugging; it won't learn down in heat or on low octane.
notes: Our data: aug30-1529 0.59 -> 0.49 with calm driving; civic11forum-60: 0.73 back to 0.49-0.51 in ~5 min. Key nuance for the app's copy: 'low rpm' helps only at light load near 0 psi; low rpm with the foot down is lugging, which raises it (g2-16, kc-oil). youtube-67's 'spirited driving speeds learning' is a single source and not used.

finding: Disconnecting the battery clears the ECU's learned data, including learned Knock Control.
log_channel: Knock Control at the start of the next drive
notes: If true, a battery disconnect should be treated like a Flash for the Unexplained-change check (a high starting score with no Flash). Not seen in our logs; keep as a note.

finding: Knock detection can be fooled by vibration and noise: rapid repeated WOT pushing Knock Control to 0.7-0.8 then back (shop theory: chassis vibration), and a loose aftermarket engine mount causing high knock counts that vanished after re-torquing.
log_channel: Knock Control before vs after a part is fitted
notes: Fits the physics already in ignition-from-datalog.md (knock-sensor signal-to-noise falls with rpm; louder exhaust raised retard in one post). Relevant to our downpipe car: a rise after fitting a part can be noise or knock and logs can't tell; the answer stays 'remove timing / check mounts and heat shields', never desensitize. civicxi-62 is an Si with an aftermarket mount (T3).

finding: Spark plugs and gap matter on tuned 1.5Ts: owners close the gap to about 0.026-0.028 in (0.7 mm); fresh plugs and oil removed audible pinging at 3-4k rpm; plug gap is the first suspect along with fuel when Knock Control creeps up at cruise.
notes: Better category: hardware-mods. No Honda plug-gap spec read in this run; civic11forum-94's '.28' is almost certainly 0.028 in. A smaller gap fights spark blow-out (misfire) under boost, which is not the same as knock. Our car shows no misfire symptom; keep out of the app until a Honda spec is read.

finding: Anti-lag and two-step live under Main Parameters / Advanced Features (two-step rpm, anti-lag ignition target, commonly -10 deg); owners warn they shorten engine life, and a cold-engine two-step blew an Si.
notes: CVT car that never launches; kc-cvt already says never brake-launch.

finding: 'Ethanol Ignition Adjustment' (MAP x RPM) adds timing on top of the ignition table at high load only, from the flex sensor.
log_channel: n/a (Flex Fuel off on this car)
notes: Our map has the tables but Flex Fuel is off and ethanol adjustments are 0 (issue 11), so they do nothing on E10 without a sensor.

finding: A cold engine reads higher Knock Control (0.53-0.55 at a 25 F start, ~0.7 at -1 C IAT) that falls to 0.49 when warm.
notes: Vietnam has no cold starts like this; our coolest start (sep01-0813) began at 0.52 and settled.

finding: Leave the knock tables alone: no reason to touch the Knock Air Limit table unless there is detonation; Si and non-Si knock sensitivity and retard tables are identical above 5,500 rpm.
ktuner_setting: Knock Air Limit (not in the owner's file); Knock_Sens_1+4 / 2+3 (forbidden)
notes: Our app already forbids every knock table (thresholds.json forbidden_tables).

finding: KTuner recommends 91+ (US AKI) for its research/Starter calibrations; low stages (16.5 psi Starter, 10th-gen Stage 0/1) can run 87, an 18 psi map on 87 works but pulls timing.
ktuner_setting: Basemap choice (Starter 21 Dual Target 2: '91+ Octane Recommended')
notes: Owner's KTuner basemap list (issue 11) reads 'Starter 21 Dual Target 2 = 21PSI. 18 PSI Target In ECO Mode. 91+ Octane Recommended.' Same as fact-check §4.

finding: Fuel below what the map wants raises Knock Control, which pulls timing everywhere and erases the tune's gain (e.g. 0.7 average on 87 vs 0.49 baseline; 0.72 on 91 vs 0.54 max on 94); better fuel steadies it.
notes: Phearable states it for its own tunes (vendors-27). On our car the tank-to-tank test already exists (kc-fuel-test).

finding: Octane labels differ: US pumps show AKI = (RON + MON) / 2, a few points below RON (RON 92 is about 88-89 AKI).
notes: Our numbers: E10 RON95 = about 90 AKI on Hondata's nominal scale (RON 90-100 ~ 85-95 AKI) and 90-91 by the usual 8-10 point RON-MON gap (kc-e10, fact-check §1); by the same arithmetic E10 RON97 III = about 92-93 AKI (our estimate, MON not published). Nuance, not yet used: ethanol widens the RON-MON gap, and boosted DI engines' knock resistance tracks RON more than MON (octane-index literature, not read in full here), so AKI probably understates E10 RON95 on this engine. That is consistent with our data (0.49-0.54 on cool pulls), but stays an inference.

finding: Off-the-shelf tunes set a fuel floor in US AKI: TSP Stage 1 requires 91/93 (93 recommended, 91 smaller gains); Phearable 93+ recommended, 91 absolute minimum, octane chosen at purchase; Axion Stage 2 needs 91.
notes: Caveat: US AKI; E10 RON95 sits at or just under every vendor's 91 floor (g2-32). A 93 file is not for Vietnamese RON95.

finding: How much octane is worth: Phearable's Si Stage 1.5 RACE dyno shows 246 hp / 291 lb-ft on a 93 file vs 234 hp / 274 lb-ft on the 91 file (about +5 % power, +6 % torque), and an SE Asia FE CVT custom tune pulled harder on RON100 than RON95.
notes: The gain comes from a separate 93 file with more timing. On one 91+ map like Starter 21 the ECU never runs more than the Ignition table, so better fuel can only return what Knock Control took (kc-timing-percent): zero on cool pulls (already at 0.49), up to ~1.6 deg in hot traffic. That is why kc-fuel-test's 'most RON97 can win back is ~1.6 deg' is right and owners should not expect the vendor's 5 %. civicxi-19 is Malaysian (CAPTS custom, RON95 E0/RON100): single owner, no log.

finding: The US fix for weak pump fuel is ethanol: a gallon or so of E85 per tank (Phearable's own instructions let a 93 file run on 91 + 1.5 gal E85) returns Knock Control to 0.49; E40 owners sit at 0.49-0.51. Too much E85 or bad blends caused lean pulls and one burnt cat.
notes: E85 is not sold at Vietnamese pumps (E10 only, E5RON92 to 2030), so the remedy translates to 'try E10 RON97 III or another busier station, tank vs tank'. civicx-81's '27 psi on E40 / 24 on E10 / 21 on pump' is a single anecdote and never a boost guide. civic11forum-25 is better filed under fuel-afr (lean 10 %+ on 87+E85).

finding: Flex-fuel facts: the stock 1.5T fuel system supports about E30 (PRL), KTuner staff recommend E30-E40 (some customers run E50); flex basemaps change fuel and ignition, not boost (~5 % gain); a Continental sensor + KTuner FFC100 converter is needed; TSP's non-flex Stage 1 tolerates up to ~15 % ethanol.
notes: No flex kit and no E85 supply here. One useful line: TSP's 15 % ethanol tolerance means E10 is inside what a non-flex vendor file expects.

finding: Enabling KTuner flex fuel on a car tuned on E10 pump gas immediately pushed fuel trims to about -7 %: the flex tables treat 0 % ethanol as the base and add fuel for the ~11 % the sensor reads in pump gas; the fix is to make E10-E11 the zero point.
basis: Data (owner log, T2) + Primary (flex table +6 % at 12 %)
notes: Category is really fuel-afr. Our pump fuel is always E10 and our trims already sit at -0.8 % median on it (kc-e10). If the owner ever fits a sensor, the flex zero point must be E10, or trims go about 6-7 % negative. Not actionable today (Flex off).

finding: Don't use octane booster: KTuner staff, Phearable and the reliability-thread curator all advise against it, and one census engine failure lists booster as a possible contributor.
notes: CivicX census raw: '1 car (a 1.5T hatch) had an engine failure where octane booster possibly contributed'; 28 users (2 %) use it. Boosters are sold in Vietnam; the app's answer to 'should I add booster?' is no, test fuels tank vs tank instead.

finding: Elevated Knock Control is usually the tank: station quality varies, mixing grades leaves sub-par fuel, and the fix is a different, busier (Top Tier) station and burning the tank off.
notes: Adds the cheap first step before buying RON97: refill at a different, high-turnover station. Heat and lugging must be ruled out first on our car (they are the measured movers).

finding: An SE Asia 2022 FE sedan CVT on KTuner V2 with a custom tune (CAPTS) ran 8,000+ km with no problems, with stable power on RON95.
notes: Closest car to ours in the crawl, but Malaysian RON95 is E0, the tune is custom, and there is no log.

finding: Intake air temperature drives Knock Control up: a shop dyno saw rises from about 98 F (37 C) intake air; 0.87 in slow traffic at 90 F+ with poor fuel vs never above 0.55 when cool; +0.10-0.15 climbing a hill in 100 F+.
notes: Our 9 drives (moving rows): IAT < 45 C -> KC p90 0.52 (max 0.57); IAT 45-64 C -> p90 0.55-0.63, max 0.65-0.70. So on this car the score starts to move from ~45 C intake, close to the shop's 37 C and to the map's IAT Ignition onset (> 40 C, kc-iat-retard). Confounded: most hot rows are the hot-traffic, lugging drive (aug30-1601). Supports the 48 C pull-start judgement in kc-heat-soak. Our +0.16 (0.49 -> 0.65) matches civicx-116's +0.10-0.15.

finding: Heat soak: intake air climbs fast in stop-and-go and when parked (91 F ambient to 143 F in short traffic; 158 F parked at 84 F ambient) and falls on the highway; at cruise IAT sits about 10 F above ambient; a centre-mounted aftermarket intake ran 130-140 F at 70 F ambient.
notes: Ours: hot restarts 57-64 C, cool drives 35-39 C moving (kc-heat-soak). youtube-58 also supports 'short-ram/centre intakes heat-soak worse' (civicx-39).

finding: 'The stock intercooler can't keep up: it saturates over multiple pulls, IAT climbs and power is cut; an intercooler is the first mod after the tune.'
basis: Consensus (10th gen, track/repeated pulls) vs our Data
log_channel: IAT minus IAT2 under boost, across back-to-back pulls
notes: Our data says otherwise for street pulls: IAT (after the IC) is only 2-11 C above IAT2 under boost, and across 8 pulls in ~7 min (aug22-0903, aug30-1529) pull-start IAT FELL (54 -> 43 C; 53 -> 45 C) with no saturation; heat soak at stops, not the core, is what costs boost (19.9 -> 16.7 psi). The forum side is 10th-gen, repeated long pulls, track and mostly hotter tunes; Phearable sells the part (vendors-40). Ours has the better basis for this car on the street. Settle: 3+ back-to-back full pulls of 4 s+ at >= 15 psi in hot afternoon air; if IAT - IAT2 grows pull to pull, the core saturates.

finding: On the 1.5T in KTuner, IAT (IAT1) is the post-intercooler sensor in the manifold (TMAP) and IAT2 is the pre-intercooler intake/MAF sensor, the reverse of Hondata's labels; KTuner logs two IAT and two ECT channels.
notes: fact-check §4 already settled it on this car's data (IAT reads 2-6 C above IAT2 under boost, impossible if IAT were before the cooler) and civicx-37 says the same for KTuner on the 1.5T. kc-iat2-side still says 'the shop never assumes which side IAT2 is on' and refuses to judge the intercooler from it: the card lags its own fact-check. Note our IAT2 tracks inlet air (pre-turbo), the forum says 'MAF (pre-intercooler)'; both are before the cooler.

finding: KTuner added IAT and ECT ignition correction (1.0.9.4); IAT ignition correction is applied through the knock ignition limit in the background.
ktuner_setting: IAT Ignition (High/Low Load Retard); ECT Retard
notes: Our map (issue 11 screenshot): IAT Ignition high-load 0 deg <= 40 C, 4.5 deg at 50 C, 9 deg at 90 C+; low load 1/3/3 deg. ECT Retard 0.8 deg at 95 C, 1.6 deg at 105 C, which kc-iat-retard does not mention yet. Edits are out-of-scope (context).

finding: The factory map lowers the turbo pressure limit as intake/engine temperature rises; KTuner relaxes but keeps the taper, so power drops as IAT2 climbs.
ktuner_setting: Turbo Pressure Limit Based On Engine Temperature (not in the owner's editable set)
notes: Already in fact-check §6 (exists, no rule uses it, effect not separable on our logs). The help page is T3 (Type R).

finding: Vendor and owner power numbers are cool-air numbers: PRL's 93-octane pull was at 65 F ambient and 73 F IAT; a dyno at ~98 F and high humidity hurt the numbers and heat-soaked the car.
notes: Expectation line for a hot-climate owner: published gains were measured in air 15-25 C cooler than a Vietnamese afternoon.

finding: A KTuner V2 LED can be mapped to IAT: yellow at 120 F (49 C), orange at 135 F (57 C), red at 145 F (63 C).
notes: His thresholds land on ours by coincidence: 49 C ~ our 48 C pull-start rule, 57-63 C ~ our hot restarts. Could become a 'set your LED' tip; category is really logging-tunerview.

finding: CivicX 10th-gen census (10/9/26): 1,704 tuned cars, 44.8 M tuned miles (~26k per car), 100 major failures (5.9 %). By current tune: Base 4.2 %, OTS 4.9 %, Custom 10.7 %; flex-fuel cars 11.8 %. CVTs: 12 failures in 580 cars (2.1 %), 5 replaced under warranty. Non-Si 6.6 %, driven by UK hatch rods; non-Si sedan/coupe 5.1 %.
basis: Forum (self-reported census, one curator; numbers checked against the raw thread)
notes: What it shows for a CVT on a base map: 95 % intervals (Wilson) CVT 1.2-3.6 %, Base 2.7-6.3 % (all models, all failure types). Of the CVT failures, listed causes are 2 brake-launch/abuse, 1 track time in 100 F weather, 1-2 likely factory defects (one on a base tune, stock setup, warranty), 1 driven hard with an emissions fault, 1 high-mileage, 1 aggressive custom flex. So heat, launching and torque, not steady pulls, which is exactly kc-cvt. Limits: no untuned control group, voluntary entries, tune type is the CURRENT tune while failures use the tune at failure (denominators don't match), per-car not per-mile, 10th-gen CVT (T2). civicx-34's older '<5 of 140' and '8 of 427' are superseded snapshots. civicx-33 (search excerpt) matches the raw exactly, so its figures can be cited from the raw. Not a safety limit; expectation only.

finding: CivicXI 11th-gen census (8/16/26): 87 tuned cars, 737k tuned miles (~8,500 per car), 1 major failure (a head gasket, 1.2 %); 21 non-Si 1.5T, 21 CVTs, no CVT failure listed. Individual 11th-gen CVTs: Starter 21 at 13,000 miles with no issues; Phearable Map 3 CVT at 32k tuned miles with no issues; one Phearable 1.5 CVT chain failure within a month (launches suspected).
notes: Too small and too young to say anything about CVT risk: 0 failures in 21 CVTs has a 95 % upper bound of ~15 %, and the average car has a third of the 10th-gen miles. civic11forum-10's chain failure is outside the census. Honest copy: 'early 11th-gen data shows no CVT failures on tuned cars, but the sample is small; the larger 10th-gen census puts tuned-CVT failures near 2 % over ~26k miles, mostly launching and heat'.

finding: Tuned CVT failures come from brake launching, launches with wheelspin and heavy low-rpm torque; never brake-launch, limit WOT from a stop, and boost-by-gear limits help protect the CVT. Base maps on unmodified, unabused cars are reported safe.
ktuner_setting: Boost_By_Gear_Limits (flat on this map; forbidden table in the app)
log_channel: Transmission Temperature; rpm jump without speed
notes: civicxi-117's 'hard to find a blown engine on an unaltered base tune' is softened by the census (a CVT failed on a base tune, stock setup, likely a factory defect). Boost-by-gear is a valid CVT protection idea but our app never writes that table; context only. civicx-36: Honda denied one CVT warranty citing the tune.

finding: Warranty: US owners report dealers must prove the tune caused a failure, yet one CVT claim was denied citing the tune and dealers can read boost history; owners flash back to stock before dealer visits; after Honda's oil-dilution ECU update owners were told to email KTuner before re-flashing.
notes: US law and dealers; Vietnam's warranty rules differ and were not read. One practical point: a Honda service ECU update overwrites the tune, so after a service visit the app should expect a 'new Flash' (score at 0.59, factory boost).

finding: Manual cars: the stock clutch is the first weak point (slip reported from ~240 lb-ft / 250-260 hp, at 22-23 psi KTuner maps, in 5th/6th; 14 % of 11th-gen Si OTS owners report minor slip); KTuner notes recommend a clutch for 22-23 psi maps; break in 600-1,000 miles; avoid flooring below 3,000-3,500 rpm; aggressive Boost Target Ramp Rate makes slip worse.
notes: Our car is a CVT. The only carry-over: the 'don't floor below ~3,000 rpm' habit, which our lugging and LSPI rules already cover (kc-oil).

finding: Engine limits on stock internals (forum): head studs and rods are the weak links; stock good to ~300 hp (one says ~350); running close to 300 lb-ft caused head-gasket seepage within months on an 11th gen; head gaskets are 30 % of non-Si engine failures in the census; upgraded head studs advised for high-output and flex setups.
notes: Our Starter 21: KTuner claims up to +79 Nm over 240 Nm, i.e. ~319 Nm (235 lb-ft), well under the ~300 lb-ft (407 Nm) where head-gasket reports start. Census raw: Honda extended the 1.5T head-gasket warranty to 10 years / 150k miles (late Aug 2026, market unstated; 'tuned cars YMMV'). Context only, never a limit.

finding: Oil dilution (fuel smell in oil) shows up on short trips and cold idling, including an Si on Starter 21 at 5,000 km after a cold snap; long drives evaporate it, and one 10th-gen oil analysis at 5 % dilution showed no extra wear.
notes: fact-check §5 already rates it a cold-climate issue of low relevance in Vietnam.

finding: Reliability-thread care rules for tuned cars: reach normal operating temperature before spirited driving; change oil and fluids sooner than the factory interval; don't go full throttle in overdriven gears (lugging); review datalogs now and then; keep a battery tender on while flashing; no VTA blow-off valves.
notes: Each line already has a home: warm engine = kc-shakedown / Drive brief checkpoint 'coolant 80 C or more'; lugging = kc-oil; fluids = kc-cvt severe schedule. New only: battery tender while flashing (a flash-day help line).

finding: A failing downpipe catalyst showed as a big mpg drop on a tuned 11th gen; bad fuel with too much E85 burnt out a cat.
notes: Symptom note for a catted-downpipe owner; our P0420 monitor is on, so a failing cat should also set the code.

finding: After fitting an intercooler or charge pipe, an under-tightened clamp let the hot-side tube blow off under boost: re-check clamps after the first drives.
notes: Fits the 'never reaches target -> boost leak' rule in owner-voices #9. Our car has no IC/charge-pipe install.
